prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and the active incretin peptide that enabled GLP-1-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: GLP-1 is the one candidate that five of six members placed first and the sixth placed third, and the scientific reasons hold up on reading all six ballots. The chain from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) to a drug class with large effects on glycemia, body weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes is mechanistically continuous and independently confirmed over three decades. It is a discovery about physiology that became medicine, which is squarely in the remit. Recognition is timely, and the evidence base (large randomized outcome trials, broad real-world use) is as mature as it gets. Holst on incretin physiology, Drucker on GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology and translation, and Mojsov on the identity and synthesis of the active peptide cover the discovery core in three names.
statement.case_against: The attribution problem is real. Habener is not among the credited names, the priority history between Mojsov, Habener and Holst is disputed, and a three-person cap excludes Knudsen, whose long-acting analogue work is what actually reached patients. A prize that stops at the peptide risks honouring discovery while leaving out the step that produced the therapy; a prize that includes Knudsen risks crediting industrial development over discovery. High opening agreement also does not equal merit, since all of us share similar recollections of the same history, and none of us has audited the priority claims.

responses.point: She also ranked GLP-1 first but proposed Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating Mojsov's role as a credit question the three-person limit leaves open.
responses.response: I disagree on the third name, though not on the prize. The Committee's tradition is to reward the discovery that opened the field, and the identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is what made the physiology tractable and the later analogue design possible. Knudsen's acylated analogues depend on that. I would put Mojsov in ahead of Knudsen, and I accept that the priority dispute means this is a judgment call rather than a settled fact. If the Committee wants a therapeutic step honoured, that is an argument for Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, but it should be made explicitly and not by default.

responses.point: He ranked the unfolded protein response first as a conceptually original, mechanistically complete pathway with thirty years of confirmation, and placed GLP-1 third.
responses.response: I agree with him on the quality of the UPR case: Walter and Mori are a clean two-person attribution and the mechanism is textbook. That is why I rank it second and name it as an alternative. Where I part company is on relative weight. The UPR's disease relevance is still largely preclinical or correlative, while GLP-1 shows the full path from mechanism to a validated clinical effect. The prize is for the greatest benefit to humankind, and on that criterion I cannot place a basic-mechanism prize above incretin therapy, though I would not oppose it in a later year.

responses.point: He ranked GLP-1 first and optogenetics second, noting that credit among six people is the main difficulty and that the prize may favour a tool over a biological finding.
responses.response: I share his worry about the attribution. Any trio leaves out Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenböck, and I cannot defend the exclusions on scientific grounds. I also think his point about tools versus findings has force here: optogenetics is a method whose medical benefit is so far small. I would therefore keep it below GLP-1, CAR-T and the UPR this year, even though its influence on research is plain.

responses.point: As chair he ranked GLP-1 first with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and described the set as his judgment of the scientific discovery core rather than a certainty.
responses.response: I agree with his proposed names and with his caution. His honesty that the allocation is a judgment is the right framing for our discussion. Where I would press is on CAR-T: he has it second with Rosenberg in the trio, while I rank Rosenberg's contribution as adjacent, since TIL and adoptive transfer are not CAR design itself, and I would keep this part in reserve for a configuration of June and Sadelain.

uncertainties: Priority among Mojsov, Habener and Holst for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is unresolved on the supplied evidence.
Whether the Committee prefers to honour discovery (Mojsov) or drug development (Knudsen) as the third laureate.
Whether CAR-T is better served by a June-Sadelain pair or needs Rosenberg and Eshhar, who is not credited.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. I have co-authored with colleagues on this Committee (Linnarsson, Frisén), but none of the shortlisted credited names is among my documented collaborators, and shared KI affiliation alone does not establish a tie.
